causebase_summary: Australian Design Centre is a Sydney-based organisation that curates and presents design exhibitions and related programs. It operates a Williams Street window gallery called Object Space, runs an Object Shop retail outlet that supports more than 150 Australian designer makers, and operates ADC On Tour travelling exhibitions that it says have toured nationally since the 1970s to provide regional Australia with access. ADC publishes Object Digital research into object and design disciplines and commissions engagement research, including a 2025 feedback survey about the impact of ADC closing. Over the last decade the centre reports it presented more than 175 exhibitions in Sydney featuring 13,200+ artists; since 2017 Object Space staged 53 exhibitions with 104 artists. People can attend exhibitions and tours, visit the shop, exhibit in Object Space, attend events and workshops, or subscribe to ADC communications.

data.Name: Australian Design Centre
data.SummaryOfActivities: The following activities were delivered in 2025:  Exhibitions and Events The 2025 creative program featured 19 exhibitions at the Centre in Sydney, up from 14 exhibitions in 2024. These included: re/JOY; PROFILE (a partnership with JMGA-NSW); Robert Foster Metal Prize (a collaboration with Craft Design Canberra); New Exuberance (a collaboration with JamFactory); MAKE Award: Biennial Prize for Innovation in Australian Craft and Design; Threads: Lore and Lineage (a collaboration with the National Indigenous Art Fair); and Crafted Liberation. Several exhibitions were presented in the window gallery including partnerships with Regional Arts NSW and Diversity Arts Australia. The Familiar in the Foreign was presented at Gallerie Handwerk in Munich and the eighth annual Sydney Craft Week Festival was presented in October 2025.  A series of events and public programs were presented alongside the exhibition programs. There were 63 events in 2025, up from 62 in 2024. The Sydney Craft Week Festival included 245 events in 2025. Audience attendance was 464,613 and above the audience attendance of 328,262 in 2024.  A total of 1,039 artists were supported through the Company s activities in 2025.  Touring  ADC On Tour is the ADC s national exhibition touring program.  Some of the nation s best contemporary craft and design exhibitions were taken to metropolitan and regional venues across the country in 2025. Three exhibitions travelled to ten museums and galleries across Australia attracting an estimated audience of 144,000 people, double the audience in 2024. These included: SIXTY: The Journal of Australian Ceramics 60th Anniversary 1962-2022; re/JOY: Vipoo Srivilasa and MAKE Award: Biennial Prize for Innovation in Australian Craft and Design. Touring exhibitions that continue beyond 2026 will be managed by other entities organised in the wind-down process in consultation with stakeholders.   Digital and Publishing  ADC continued to raise its digital profile through the development of content across website and social media channels for local and global audiences. Website and social media platforms had an online audience of over 334,000 (2024: 289,000).   In publishing a major monograph, The Story So Far: Helen Britton was co-published with Arnoldsche to accompany the exhibition which launched in August 2025 before a national tour to follow from 2026-2028.
